title: land's branch-step refusal names the process it found in the worker's worktree, so an orchestrator can tell its own shell from a worker
goal: when backlog.py land stops at the branch step because a process runs in the worker's worktree, the refusal prints that process's command and whether it belongs to the calling session's own process tree, so an orchestrator whose shell sits in that worktree moves out instead of waiting for a worker that has ended

run: import sys;t=open('_tools/bl_land.py',encoding='utf-8').read();sys.exit(0 if 'own shell' in t or 'calling session' in t else 1)
